outcome: Upper esophageal sphincter (UES) characteristics (nadir pressure, contractile reflex)
cohort: Thirty-eight infants (mean 28.0 +/- 0.7 weeks gestation) with aerodigestive morbidities such as dysphagia, life-threatening events, aspiration-pneumonia, atelectasis, and reflux.
finding: Aerodigestive reflexes were similarly developed in infants using noninvasive respiratory support with adequate upper and lower aerodigestive protection, though NC or nCPAP groups experienced delayed feeding milestones and altered esophageal motility compared to room air.
cross-section timing: At a mean gestational age of 28.0 +/- 0.7 weeks
